title: Add up the headroom first
statement: Before committing to an overall target, add up each item type's realistic headroom to see whether the target can be reached and which type decides it.
example: With every other type near its ceiling, the weakest type at its best-ever rate gave 83.8% overall against a 95% target.
detail: Per-type arithmetic on measured pass rates was written into the project's target file as something to read before approving any spend (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/mission_locked_95_aggregate.md`). A 95% target meant 282 of 297 prompts passing; with every other type near its estimated ceiling, the weakest type at its best-ever rate gave 249 of 297 (83.8%), and at an 80% pass rate 276 of 297 (92.9%). That made the weakest type the binding constraint.
against: The per-type ceilings are estimates ("maybe 8-10", `icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/mission_locked_95_aggregate.md`, line 37). The +47 for the other types sits inside the 41 to 52 range the table implies, and even at 52, with the weakest type at 80%, the total is 281, one short of 282.

evidence.quote: **Without solving DBQ:** non-DBQ ceilings at +47, DBQ at all-time-best +11 = **+58 max**. 191 + 58 = **249/297 = 83.8%.** Below bar.
**With DBQ at 80% pass rate (24+24=48 vs current 10):** +38 from DBQ + +47 from non-DBQ = +85. **191 + 85 = 276/297 = 92.9%.** Still below bar.
**The strict variety cap (match ≤6/15) is unreachable regardless of Claude** — a structural non-match shortage (623 available vs 729 needed), not a wiring bug.
